gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ALLPOWERS S2000, the only kit at exactly 1,500 Wh, uses a ternary lithium (NCM) battery and limits solar input to 500 W (MPPT 12–70 V, 18 A). ALLPOWERS sells the S2000 Pro kit at the same price, and its US store lists the Pro at 1,000 W maximum solar input through XT60.
standout_why: I compared against stormwatts.com (cited) and powersized.com/solar-generator-kits (cited). StormWatts gives solar-input caps, voltage windows and wiring rules for Jackery 1000/2000/HomePower, EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus/Max/Ultra, BLUETTI and Anker. It has no ALLPOWERS model and no 1,500 Wh-class station. PowerSized lists the Jackery 1500 v2 and 1500 Ultra kits but no solar current or voltage limit for the Explorer 1500 series, and no ALLPOWERS. Neither page names the battery chemistry of any ~1,500 Wh kit. I could not open our own cited page (dealectric.com/solar-generator-with-panels-included) because of a TLS error, so I have not compared against it.
decides: This settles the choice among our ~1,500 Wh rows. On 2026-11-17, ALLPOWERS listed the S2000 and S2000 Pro kits at the same price with each panel: $681.00 with SF200, $1,043.10 with SP037. The S2000 has NCM cells and a 500 W solar cap, and its kits are pre-orders dispatching Nov 20, 2026. The S2000 Pro kit has 1,000 W solar input and 2,400 W AC, and with SP037 or SE100/SE200 it ships now. The S2000 Pro + SP037 400 W kit is therefore our pick for this size. The S2000 kit only makes sense if a pre-order is acceptable, and it is not cheaper. The SP037 panel alone is rated 37.4 V, and a single panel fits both stations' input windows. I could not source the Jackery 1500 v2 solar limits from an opened page, so I have no mechanism finding for it either way.
candidates: Jackery Solar Generator 1500 v2 (Explorer 1500 v2 + 2× SolarSaga 100 Air)
